title: Revelation 17:1–6
context: An angel shows John the judgment of the great prostitute who sits on many waters. She rides a scarlet beast with seven heads and ten horns, is dressed in luxury, and bears the name Babylon the Great, mother of prostitutes. She is drunk with the blood of the saints and martyrs of Jesus.

verses.text: One of the seven angels who had the seven bowls came and spoke with me, saying, “Come here. I will show you the judgment of the great prostitute who sits on many waters,
verses.arminianNotes: The great prostitute is introduced. Her judgment is the subject of chapters 17 and 18.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the world’s seductive power opposed to God.

verses.text: with whom the kings of the earth committed sexual immorality. Those who dwell on the earth were made drunken with the wine of her sexual immorality.”
verses.arminianNotes: The kings of the earth committed immorality with her, and the world was made drunk with her wine. Immorality is a frequent biblical image for idolatry.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see idolatry and economic seduction joined.

verses.text: He carried me away in the Spirit into a wilderness. I saw a woman sitting on a scarlet-colored beast, full of blasphemous names, having seven heads and ten horns.
verses.arminianNotes: She sits on a scarlet beast full of blasphemous names.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the alliance of seductive culture and hostile power.

verses.text: The woman was dressed in purple and scarlet, and decked with gold and precious stones and pearls, having in her hand a golden cup full of abominations and the impurities of the sexual immorality of the earth.
verses.arminianNotes: She is dressed in purple and scarlet with gold and a cup full of abominations.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the attraction of worldly glory.

verses.text: And on her forehead a name was written, “MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF THE PROSTITUTES AND OF THE ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH.”
verses.arminianNotes: Her name is Babylon the Great. Preterists and many others see Rome; historicists in the Reformation era often saw papal Rome; futurists may see a revived world system; idealists see the world’s seduction in every age.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that older Protestant writers often identified her with papal Rome, while many today see Rome in John’s day and the world system more broadly.

verses.text: I saw the woman drunken with the blood of the saints and with the blood of the martyrs of Jesus. When I saw her, I wondered with great amazement.
verses.arminianNotes: She is drunk with the blood of the saints. John is astonished.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see persecution as characteristic of the world opposed to God.
